# BC Tribunal Confirms Companies Remain Liable for Information Provided by AI Chatbot
Authors
8-10 分鐘
Business Law Today

February 2024

Lisa R Lifshitz and Roland Hung
Summary

    In Moffatt v. Air Canada, the British Columbia Civil Resolution Tribunal found Air Canada liable for misinformation given to a consumer by an AI chatbot on its website and awarded damages.
    The AI chatbot provided the consumer with incorrect information about the airline’s policy for discounted bereavement fares. When the consumer submitted his application for a partial refund following the chatbot’s information, Air Canada refused.
    The Tribunal found in favor of the consumer’s claim of negligent misrepresentation. Though Air Canada endeavored to argue that the chatbot was a separate legal entity responsible for its own actions, the Tribunal found that Air Canada still bore responsibility for all the information on its website, whether it came from a static page or a chatbot.
    While admittedly this is not a court decision, the Tribunal’s decision in Moffatt serves as a helpful reminder that companies remain liable for the actions of their AI tools and should put into place adequate internal policies for their accuracy and other considerations.

On February 14, 2024, the British Columbia Civil Resolution Tribunal (the “Tribunal”) found Air Canada liable for misinformation given to a consumer through the use of artificial intelligence chatbots (“AI chatbot”).

The decision, Moffatt v. Air Canada, generated international headlines, with reports spanning from the Washington Post in the United States to the BBC in the United Kingdom. While AI comes with economical and functional benefits, companies clearly remain liable if inaccurate information is provided to consumers through use of an AI tool.

Background

AI chatbots are automated programs that use AI and other potential tools like natural language processing to simulate a conversation and provide information in response to a person’s prompts and input. Common virtual assistants such as Alexa and Siri are all examples of AI chatbots.

Increasingly, AI chatbots are used in commerce. According to a 2024 report from AI Multiple Research, AI chatbots have saved organizations around $0.70 USD per interaction. By 2025, the predicted revenue of the chatbot industry is estimated to reach around $1.3 billion USD. Today, around half of all large companies are considering investing in these tools. Air Canada’s AI chatbot is one example of their use in a commercial setting. However, as the Tribunal’s decision shows, they do not come without risks.
The Tribunal’s Decision in Moffatt

The Tribunal’s decision came after a complaint was made by Jake Moffatt. Moffatt wanted to purchase an Air Canada plane ticket to fly to Ontario, where his grandmother had recently passed away. On the airline’s website, Moffatt engaged with an AI chatbot, which responded that there is a discount if the buyer is traveling because of a death in the family and using reduced bereavement fares. Anyone seeking a reduced fare could allegedly submit their ticket within ninety days of issuance through an online form and receive the lower bereavement rate.

Unfortunately, the AI chatbot’s answer was incorrect. The reference to “bereavement fares” was hyperlinked to a separate Air Canada webpage titled “Bereavement travel” that contained additional information regarding Air Canada’s bereavement policy. The webpage indicated that the bereavement policy does not apply to requests for bereavement consideration after travel was completed. Accordingly, when Moffatt submitted his application to receive a partial refund of his fare, Air Canada refused. After a series of interactions, Air Canada admitted that the chatbot had provided “misleading words.” The representative pointed out the chatbot’s link to the bereavement travel webpage and said Air Canada had noted the issue so it could update the chatbot.

Moffatt then sued Air Canada for having relied on its chatbot, which the Tribunal determined was an allegation of negligent misrepresentation. Air Canada alleged that the correct information could have been found elsewhere on its website and argued that it could not be liable for the AI chatbot’s responses. Strangely, Air Canada endeavored to argue that the chatbot was a separate legal entity that is responsible for its own actions.

The Tribunal ultimately found in favor of Moffatt. While a chatbot has an interactive component, the Tribunal found that the program was just a part of Air Canada’s website and Air Canada still bore responsibility for all the information on its website, whether it came from a static page or a chatbot. As a service provider, Air Canada owed Moffatt a duty of care that was breached by the misrepresentation. Air Canada could not separate itself from the AI chatbot, which was integrated in its own website. Negligence existed as Air Canada did not take reasonable care to ensure that its chatbot provided accurate information. It did not matter if the correct information existed elsewhere. A consumer cannot be expected to double-check information it finds on one part of the website with another.

The Tribunal ultimately awarded Moffat approximately $650 CAD in damages, plus pre-judgement interest and filing fees with the Tribunal.
Takeaways

While admittedly this is not a court decision, the Tribunal’s decision in Moffatt serves as a helpful reminder that companies remain liable for the actions of their AI tools. Additionally, any company that intends to use AI tools should also ensure that they also put into place adequate internal policies that protect consumer privacy, warn consumers of any limitations, and train the AI system to deliver accurate results.

    Moffatt v. Air Canada, 2024 BCCRT 149.

    Kyle Melnick, “Air Canada chatbot promised a discount. Now the airline has to pay it.,” Washington Post, February 18, 2024; Maria Yagoda, “Airline held liable for its chatbot giving passenger bad advice – what this means for travellers,” BBC, February 23, 2024.

    “What is a chatbot?,” IBM, accessed February 27, 2024.

    Cem Dilmegani, “90+ Chatbot/Conversational AI Statistics in 2024,” AIMultiple, last modified February 5, 2024.

    Moffatt, supra note 1, at paras. 13-16.

    Id. at paras. 18–25.

    Id. at paras. 26–32.

# BC 司法委員會確認公司對人工智慧聊天機器人提供的資訊仍需負責

作者 Lisa R Lifshitz & Roland Hung｜8-10 分鐘閱讀時間｜《商業法律今日》

2024 年 2 月

英國哥倫比亞普通法上訴法院在 **Moffatt v. Air Canada** 一案中裁定，加拿大航空（Air Canada）因其網站上的人工智慧聊天機器人提供的錯誤資訊對消費者負有責任，並判賠損失。該 AI 聊天機器人在回覆消費者關於折扣哀悼票價政策的詢問時給出不實訊息。當消費者依據聊天機器人的資訊申請部分退款時，加拿大航空拒絕了申請。

雖然加拿大航空試圖辯稱該聊天機器人是一個獨立法律實體，負責自己的行動，但法院認為該公司仍需對其網站上的所有資訊負全責，無論這些資訊來自靜態頁面還是由 AI 聊天機器人提供。這項裁決雖非最終判決，但提醒企業必須為其 AI 工具的準確性及其他考量建立足夠的內部政策。

2024 年 2 月 14 日，英國哥倫比亞普通法上訴法院（以下簡稱「司法委員會」）在 **Moffatt v. Air Canada** 一案中裁定，加拿大航空需為其透過人工智慧聊天機器人提供給消費者的錯誤資訊負責。

此判決——**Moffatt v. Air Canada**——在國際間引發關注，從美國的《華盛頓郵報》到英國的 BBC 均有報導。《紐約時報》指出：「AI 技術帶來經濟與功能上的優勢，但若公司透過 AI 工具向消費者提供錯誤資訊，仍需承擔責任。」此案凸顯出企業在運用 AI 技術時應特別留意其準確性及相關風險。

背景說明：
人工智慧聊天機器人是利用 AI 及其他工具（如自然語言處理）自動化的程式，旨在模擬對話並根據使用者的提示與輸入提供資訊。Alexa 與 Siri 等常見虛擬助理即為此類 AI 聊天機器的例子。

越來越多地，AI 客服正被應用於商業領域。根據 2024 年 AI Multiple Research 的報告指出，AI 客服已為組織節省了約每互動次數 0.70 美元。預計到 2025 年，聊天機器人產業的收入將達到約 13 億美元。目前，大約一半的大型公司正在考慮投資這些工具。加拿大航空的 AI 客服就是其中一個商業應用的例子。然而，如 Tribunal 的裁決所示，這類系統並非沒有風險。

《Moffatt 案》中的裁決即是如此。投訴人 Jake Moffatt 希望購買一張飛往安大略省的 Air Canada 機票，以前往他最近去世的祖母位於該地的住所。在航空公司網站上，Moffatt 與 AI 客服互動，客服回應說如果購票者因家人離世而旅行，則適用折扣。任何希望獲得減免票價的人據稱可以在票務發出後 90 天內透過線上表單提交申請，並獲得較低的喪葬優惠費率。

然而，AI 客服的答案是錯誤的。客服提到的「喪葬優惠票價」實際上指向一個獨立的 Air Canada 頁面——《喪葬旅行》，該頁面包含有關 Air Canada 喪葬政策的其他資訊。該頁面指出，喪葬政策不適用於完成行程後申請的減免考量。因此，當 Moffatt 提交他的部分退款申請時，Air Canada 以此為由拒絕了。在多次互動之後，Air Canada 才承認 AI 客服提供的答案是「誤導性文字」。客服人員指出該連結指向喪葬旅行頁面，並表示 Air Canada 已注意到問題，以便更新聊天機器人。

隨後，Moffatt 控告 Air Canada 依賴其 AI 客服，而 Tribunal 裁定這項行為構成過失的錯誤陳述。《Air Canada 航空》則主張正確資訊可以在其網站的其他地方找到，並辯稱不應為 AI 客服的回覆負責。有趣的是，《Air Canada 航空》試圖論證該聊天機器人是一個獨立的法律實體，應對自身行為負責。

The Tribunal ultimately found in favor of Moffatt. 雖然聊天機器人具有互動功能，但 Tribunal 認定該程式僅為 Air Canada 網站的一部分，而 Air Canada 對其網站上的所有資訊仍負有責任，無論是來自靜態頁面還是聊天機器人。作為服務提供者，Air Canada 因誤導而對 Moffatt 構成注意義務的違反。由於 AI 聊天機器人已整合到其自身網站中，Air Canada 無法將自己與聊天機器人分離。疏忽存在於 Air Canada 未採取合理措施確保其聊天機器人提供的資訊準確。無論正確資訊是否存在於其他地方，消費者都不應被期望對其在網站某一部分找到的資訊進行二次確認。

最終，Tribunal 判決 Moffatt 勝訴，並約 $650 CAD 的損害賠償、預審利息和法院費用。

**重點提醒**
雖然這不是法院判決，但 Tribunal 在 Moffatt 案中的決定提供了一個有用的提醒：公司仍需對其 AI 工具的行為負責。此外，任何打算使用 AI 工具的公司都應確保制定足夠的內部政策來保護消費者隱私、告知消費者有關限制，並訓練 AI 系統以提供準確結果。

Moffatt v. Air Canada, 2024 BCCRT 149.
Kyle Melnick，「Air Canada 聊天機器人承諾折扣。現在航空公司必須支付。」《華盛頓郵報》，2024 年 2 月 18 日；Maria Yagoda，「航空業因其聊天機器人提供錯誤建議而被認定有責任——這對旅客意味著什麼？」BBC，2024 年 2 月 23 日。
「什麼是聊天機器人？」（IBM，2024 年 2 月 27 日）
Cem Dilmegani，「2024 年聊天機器人和對話式 AI 的 90+ 資料統計」，AIMultiple，最後修改日期：2024 年 2 月 5 日。
Moffatt，supra note 1，第 13–16 段；
同上，第 18–25 段；
同上，第 26–32 段。
